requirement:
An mdBook chapter MAY declare a named definition using a fenced `{definition}` directive. Definitions MUST use the same chapter-qualified names, identifier rules, fence rules, and nonempty-body rules as requirements and examples. Names MUST be unique across all three kinds.

Each definition MUST declare exactly one nonempty `:phrase:` option before its explanatory body. The phrase MUST be interpreted as plain text. Definitions MUST NOT require their own evidence records or determinations.
rationale:
I found no gap against `requirements.definitions.declaration`.

**Shared name, identifier, fence and nonempty-body rules.**
- `src/lib.rs#fn[definition_blocks]` parses `{definition}` blocks with the same fence-length and closing logic as `{req}` and `{example}`. It also applies the same `valid_name` check.
- `src/evidence.rs#fn[collect_definitions]` reports these errors for definitions exactly as for the other kinds, with the kind noun "definition":
  - invalid or reserved names;
  - a missing closing fence;
  - empty text ("has no text").
- An invalid name declares nothing, but the fence and body checks still run.
- `src/lib.rs#fn[preprocess_book]` skips invalid and unclosed blocks.
- Tests:
  - `tests/definitions.rs#fn[definitions_share_name_and_fence_rules_and_need_no_evidence]` covers the invalid chapter-qualified name `bad dir.terms.a` and the longer-fence body.
  - `tests/definitions.rs#fn[invalid_declarations_and_reference_targets_are_reported]` covers the missing closing fence.

**Uniqueness across all three kinds.**
- `collect_definitions` keeps one `BTreeMap` entry per name across all kinds, and a second declaration produces "duplicate definition …; first declared at …".
- The test `invalid_declarations_and_reference_targets_are_reported` declares requirement `x` and then definition `x`, and asserts "duplicate definition bad.x".

**Exactly one nonempty `:phrase:` before the body.**
- `collect_definitions` does not parse options for definitions, so `:phrase:` stays in the text. It then calls `src/terms.rs#fn[declaration]`.
- `declaration` requires the first line to be a nonempty `:phrase:`, requires a nonempty body, and rejects a second `:phrase:` that immediately starts the body.
- The test `invalid_declarations_and_reference_targets_are_reported` covers four cases:
  - no phrase;
  - empty phrase;
  - duplicate phrases;
  - phrase with no body.
- It asserts the error "definition bad.bad:" for each.

**Phrase interpreted as plain text.**
- `preprocess_book` renders the phrase through `replace_definitions` and `replace_inline_references`, which call `terms::escaped_phrase`. That function escapes Markdown metacharacters and HTML.
- The test `tests/definitions.rs#fn[phrases_are_plain_links_and_markdown_literals_are_preserved]` asserts that `*alpha* & <beta>` renders as `*alpha* & <beta>`.

**No evidence records or determinations required.**
- In `src/evidence.rs#fn[inspect_repository_with_progress]`, the expected-evidence lookup and the "missing" loop both exclude `DefinitionKind::Term`.
- Authoring, status and info selection all filter out `DefinitionKind::Term`, so definitions never become subjects for determinations. Examples are `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[select_subjects]` and `src/commands.rs#fn[status_markdown_with_github]`.
- The test `definitions_share_name_and_fence_rules_and_need_no_evidence` asserts there is no "missing evidence" error for the glossary definitions. It also asserts the error `evidence/rules.ready.json: missing` for the requirement, so the check is not vacuous.

Every obligation has an `{impl}` item and at least one `{test}` that runs it. The unspecified-behavior check turned up nothing outside the text.
